title: Pro-etale evaluation over an algebraically closed field
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Z=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-scheme]. The functor $S\mapsto Z[S]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] identifies sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with sheaves on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings. Under this identification, the inverse image $p_Z^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] is the identity on sheaves on profinite sets, and evaluation at $Z$ is evaluation at the one-point profinite set. Every pro-etale covering of $Z$ admits a section through one member. Evaluation at $Z$ is exact on abelian sheaves, and on sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over any ring sheaf $R$ it preserves finite free modules and cokernels, with values in modules over $R(Z)$. For every extension $K\subseteq K'$ of algebraically closed fields, scheme inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] corresponds to the identity under these profinite-site identifications, and therefore canonically preserves evaluation at the final object. These identifications are compatible with composition and with ring and module structures.
